phenomenon_scale.description: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Ambulocetus natans (224 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.formation_note: Kuldana Formation, Pakistan; amphibious archaeocete with large hind limbs (Thewissen, Hussain and Arif 1994)

equations.schnakenberg: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + D_u laplacian(u); dv/dt = b - u^2 v + D_v laplacian(v)
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = largest eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)

parameters.note: Dimensionless Schnakenberg rates. gamma multiplies both reaction and diffusion so k is unchanged and the pattern saturates in fewer wall-clock steps. These values are for the 224 µm detail slot and are not the 1 cm sibling parameters.

boundary_conditions: Periodic boundaries on the square primordium patch. The flank inset on the fossil photograph is a window onto that patch, not a no-flux bone surface.
empirical_claims: Thewissen, Hussain and Arif (1994) name Ambulocetus natans and argue from the skeleton for amphibious, foot-powered swimming in the early middle Eocene of Pakistan.
Turing (1952) showed that two diffusing morphogens can be stable without diffusion and unstable at a finite wavenumber.
Schnakenberg (1979) gave the activator-inhibitor kinetics used here.
Kondo and Miura (2010) review reaction-diffusion as a framework for stripes, spots and related pigment patterns. No dermal wavelength is published for Ambulocetus.

Thewissen et al. (2001) place Pakicetus as a terrestrial cetacean; Gingerich et al. (1994) place Rodhocetus as a more aquatic swimmer. The hydration factors 0.72 and 1.35 are a transfer hypothesis of this script, not measurements from those papers.

specimen.credit: Own work. Fossil of Ambulocetus photographed at Naturalis Biodiversity Center, Leiden.

does_not_claim: That pigment stripes or ocelli are preserved on the Naturalis mount.
That 224 µm was measured on a fossil skin.
That Pakicetus or Rodhocetus wavelengths were measured; h = 0.72 and h = 1.35 are reconstructions.
